title: How I Accidentally Broke Reality Fracture Draft!
event: FRA early access / preview event (he thanks Wizards for free preview access at 0:04-0:08 'so I could get this recorded early'; Premier / Quick not named on screen)
source: frames read from data/videos/raw/97ZjOdFNU4U (banner, pack grids and title strips every pick; pool at P2p3 and P3p1; deck builder at 17:48); every pack list read from images that loaded except the last card of pack 3 (never displayed, inferred); takes confirmed by the pool and the deck builder (all 42 picks accounted for: 23 main spells, Theorix Annex, 17 in the sideboard, and the picked Mountain among the free basics); transcript from YouTube auto captions, card names corrected against the dataset; nothing past 17:50 read; the cut-off is 1075 s (game board at 1110 s)

picks.reasoning: Null Summoner: excellent and very powerful every time he has played it; it does not scale into the late game, but usually the opponent holds something, you take their best card and trade the 4/2 for one creature, a clean two-for-one. Several scary cards in the pack (Samut) but he takes the gold rare.

considered.Samut, Hazoret's Champion: a scary card when the opponent plays it
considered.Proft, Consulting Detective: pretty solid, he thought it would be a bit better; the minus three / minus one early is decent
considered.Fulminous Forte: has been excellent, one damage plus a kill makes the game feel over
considered.Fatehold Chronologist: a mover down for him, still fine

quotes: Null Summoner is excellent. It has been very, very powerful every time I've been able to play it.
You take their best card and trade this for one other creature. Really, really strong.

picks.reasoning: Memory Trap over Vigorbloom Vanguard: he reads from the missing card that the pack lost a blue or red card (the blue Traxos is not in it), thinks of a splash, and locks up a kill spell. He prefers being the one asking the questions rather than answering them, but there is no good follow-up to Null Summoner.

considered.Vigorbloom Vanguard: a very flexible card at the very least
considered.Traxos, Scourge Eternal: its blue partner is missing, so the neighbour probably took a blue or red card

picks.plan: Open; Null Summoner plus a possible white-black splash card.
quotes: let's just take the memory trap. It's good to get a kill spell locked up
I have been kind of thinking that in this format, I want to be the one asking the questions rather than trying to answer them a lot of the time.

picks.reasoning: Mindseeker Oculus 'is just the pick': super good, he has been impressed every time he has played it; he accepts the neighbour might move into blue and cut him. The missing card in this pack (Teyo pairs with black, Marwyn with green) points to a black or green card taken; white is neither colour.

considered.Teyo, Lightshield Expert: very impressive when he gets to do his thing
considered.Icy Reception: a mover down for him; a card you want one copy of; may get better as formats speed up, but games have stalled out

picks.plan: Open; blue Oculus alongside the gold start.
quotes: I think the Oculus is just the pick. Just super good card.
got to just take the cards that I am presented with.

picks.reasoning: Grim Repriser (black-red gold), the best card in the pack, over Wrath of the Bloodmane and the rest: he will be flexible and dabble, multicoloured cards are strong and a different lane from his current one.
picks.plan: Open, flexible; blue-black base with a gold dabble.
quotes: I'm going to try taking the Grim Repriser. I think it's just the best card in the pack. And I'm willing to be flexible here and just dabble.

picks.reasoning: Hapatra, the Desert Fang: he takes multicoloured cards pretty highly right now because in his experience they are the best card in your deck or one of them, which is worth speculating on; the rest of the pack is weak.
quotes: I'm just going to take the multicolored cards pretty highly right now. In my experience, they're just so strong and they can be like the best card in your deck or one of them.
This pack is just kind of weak other than Hapatra though.

picks.reasoning: A second Mindseeker Oculus: he has jumped around but could be a blue-black deck splashing green. He has come down on Arni, Humble Scribe: a three-drop you do not want to block with is a liability, and that was costing him games.

considered.Arni, Humble Scribe: has come down on it; a three-drop you don't want to block with is a liability and was costing him games

quotes: we could just be like a blue black deck splashing green.
I've come down on Arni because like playing a three drop that you don't want to block with is just kind of a liability sometimes.

picks.reasoning: Extended Absence: blue-black looking like it could be open. He does not want to splash red for Grim Repriser; Paradox Shaper has been fine and Heartstring Puller is still in the pack.
quotes: Now I get an extended absence. So blue black looking like it could be open.
I don't really want to splash red for Grim Repriser.

picks.reasoning: Paradox Shaper over Undulating Witness and Silence the Echo: he needs more twos and has no good one; it helps fill the graveyard and get the synergies going.
quotes: Think I need more twos. I don't really have a good one. And this card can be fine. Helps you fill your graveyard.

picks.reasoning: Bestial Incursion (green) from a thin pack: 'sometimes fine'; he does not like another card in the pack and is not the biggest fan of Keeper of the Quiet Hour.
picks.plan: Blue-black; green still a possible splash colour.
quotes: Bestial Incursion is sometimes fine.

picks.reasoning: Keeper of the Quiet Hour from a weak pack (Identity Echo, Essence Burn, Traxos, Scourge Eternal, Keeper, Swamp): he says he has not been the biggest fan of it.
quotes: Have not been the biggest fan of Keeper of the Quiet Hour.

picks.reasoning: Solve for Disappointment: it has been a little obnoxious, so he will try it (empower Jace 1 plus discard); Frostbite Pyromental and Skilled Battlecarver are the alternatives.
quotes: Solve for disappointment has been a little bit obnoxious though. So maybe we'll try that.

picks.reasoning: Void Extrapolator over Sphinx's Approach: as a two-drop to help his synergies; he thought it pretty decent. He sees black as open: the late Extended Absence, and blue-black could just be played.
quotes: I have thought void extrapolator was pretty decent. So just as a two drop to help seal your synergies.
it's looking like black is open here. We got the late extended absence. We could just play blue black.

picks.reasoning: Extrapolate the Impossible over Island: no comment; the pack gives nothing else.
Last card, Mountain, auto-picked.

Diviner of Victory, an 'okay rare': not great but it will be okay, maybe just a cheap play to get on board early. At the start of the pack he notes black looks open and he does not have to be blue; white did not seem open, red did not seem open (he took Grim Repriser and saw no good red cards, second-picked Memory Trap and saw no good white).

considered.Yuriko, Hope from the Shadows: in the pack, wheels at pick 9

picks.plan: Blue-black: black open, 'we don't actually have to be blue'.
quotes: This card seems like it's an okay rare. It's not great, but it'll be okay. Maybe just a cheap play. Get on board early.
black is looking open. We don't actually have to be blue, though.

picks.reasoning: Traxos, Academy Guardian: 'love me the Traxos'; Codie lets you copy prepared spells, and Traxos has been very, very strong. Blessed Ghoul is fine; raw card draw is fine sometimes; blue-black dreams live.
quotes: Love me the Traxos.
Traxos has been very very strong.

picks.reasoning: Mabel, Bitter Recluse (his first copy): a very strong deathtoucher that can sometimes kill Jaces. Eye of Jace was good in a blue-white surveil tempo aggro deck he had; Mabel, Valley Hero is pretty good; Paradox Shaper is fine.

considered.Eye of Jace: was pretty good in a blue-white surveil tempo aggro deck: 'this card's really strong'

quotes: Mabel very strong death toucher that can sometimes kill Jaces.
Just going to nab my first copy of Mabel. It's pretty nice to get this one.

picks.reasoning: Vraska's Final Mercy: either a draw two for two mana or a kill spell for two mana, a flexible spell; the blue-black land (Theorix Annex) is in the pack but he is happy to get the flexible spell.

considered.Theorix Annex: blue-black land in the pack; he would rather have the flexible spell

quotes: I do like Vraska's Final Mercy. It's either like a draw spell. It's like a draw two for two mana or kill spell for two mana.
I think I'm just happy you're getting the flexible spell.

picks.reasoning: Recursive Recruitment: really does a lot of work in the late game; Gallia is also pretty nice.
quotes: I really do like recursive recruitment. I think Gallia is also pretty nice, but this card really just does a lot of work in the late game.

picks.reasoning: Theoretical Necromancer, the three-drop, over Protege's Awakening (he has not been impressed by it but wonders whether he is misvaluing it). He does not think he wants to play Grim Repriser and would rather splash green, but might not splash at all.

considered.Protege's Awakening: has not been impressed, maybe he is misvaluing it
considered.Grim Repriser: does not think he wants to play it; would rather splash green

quotes: I'll take the three drop. I've not been that impressed by the Protege's Awakening, but maybe it's just that I'm misvaluing things.
I don't think I want to play the Grim Repriser. I'd rather splash green, but I might not splash at all.

picks.reasoning: Recursive Recruitment number two: glad he took a cheaper card there and glad he took Mabel for more defensive options; his deck now has a real (garbled) plan.
quotes: Recursive Recruitment number two. I'm glad I took a cheaper card there. I'm also glad I took this Mabel and just more defensive options.

picks.reasoning: Yuriko, Hope from the Shadows over Solve for Disappointment, Icy Reception and Wrath of the Bloodmane; no spoken reason for the take (the pool at P3p1 shows Yuriko, Hope, taken here or at the wheel; Apex Witchstalker at pick 9 fits the transcript). the more playables I get, the less likely I am to want to splash because especially in a self-milled deck, sometimes splashing is a little bit just dicey.
